learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the science of heat! Explore how temperature scales work, why things expand when heated, and the physics behind melting ice and boiling water.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold something is (average kinetic energy). Heat is the actual energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference. Heat always flows naturally from hot to cold.

Most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled (Linear, Area, and Volume expansion). However, Water is weird! It has 'Anomalous Expansion'—it actually shrinks when heated from $0^\circ C$ to $4^\circ C$, making it densest at $4^\circ C$.

The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by $1^\circ C$. Water has an incredibly high specific heat, which is why it takes a long time to boil and a long time to cool down.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧊 Change of State and Latent Heat
main_concepts.simple_explanation: When ice melts or water boils, the temperature stops changing! The heat you apply is used entirely to break molecular bonds, changing the state. This hidden energy is called Latent Heat.

main_concepts.concept_title: ♨️ Heat Transfer & Newton's Law of Cooling
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Heat transfers via Conduction (solids touching), Convection (fluids circulating), or Radiation (electromagnetic waves in vacuum). Newton's Law says a hot body cools down faster if the surrounding room is very cold.

fun_activity.title: 🥶 The Metal vs. Wood Illusion
fun_activity.instructions: Touch a metal spoon and a wooden table in the same room. The metal feels much colder! But they are exactly the same temperature. Metal is just a fantastic thermal conductor, so it rapidly steals the heat away from your skin, tricking your brain into feeling 'cold'.

exam_tips: 📌 The Principle of Calorimetry (Heat Lost = Heat Gained) is a standard numerical where you usually have to find the final equilibrium temperature of mixing hot copper with cold water.

📌 Know why anomalous expansion of water is crucial for survival: Because ice is less dense than water, lakes freeze from the top down, insulating the liquid water below so fish can survive the winter!
📌 Wien's Displacement Law ($\lambda_{max} T = b$) proves why hotter stars appear blue and cooler stars appear red.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Kelvin scale is the absolute temperature scale; $0 \text{ K}$ is absolute zero where all molecular motion stops.
⭐ Black bodies are both perfect absorbers and perfect emitters of thermal radiation.
⭐ Burns caused by steam at $100^\circ C$ are much more severe than boiling water at $100^\circ C$ due to the massive Latent Heat of vaporization.
